label: Button Group
title: Button Group
summary: Keep a few related actions in one row with shared spacing and modes.
corePrinciple: Give the group its width and modes; let only the key action stand out.

anatomy.title: A row that spaces and sizes its children
anatomy.description: ButtonGroup has no surface of its own. It places its children in one row, separates them with a token gap, and decides which children stretch.
blocks: Fills the width its host provides, centers children vertically, and adds no padding or background.
A direct IconButton child keeps its own circular size instead of stretching.
One token gap, buttonGroup/gap, separates every pair of neighbors.
Every Button child stretches, so the Buttons share the remaining width equally.

configuration.title: Choose the children; the group lays them out
configuration.description: ButtonGroup exposes no layout options. The children you place and the modes you set on the group decide what people see.
blocks: Each IconButton keeps its size. The row starts at the leading edge and leaves the rest of the host empty.
The icon keeps its size and the two Buttons split what remains.
Both Buttons stretch to equal halves of the row.
The modes selected on the Figma master. Every child inherits them from the group.
Changing the group modes changes every child together: smaller controls and stronger fills.

states.title: State belongs to each child
states.description: ButtonGroup has no enabled, disabled, or selected state of its own. Each child keeps its own disabled, hover, and pressed feedback.
blocks: Every child resolves the group’s modes and responds on its own.
The disabled Button fades to half opacity and ignores presses. It keeps its share of the row, so the layout does not shift.

sizing.title: The host sets the width
sizing.description: ButtonGroup fills the width it receives. IconButtons keep their size and Buttons divide the rest, so a narrow host can shorten labels.
blocks: Each Button has room for its full label.
The equal share is narrower than “Request”, so the label ends in an ellipsis.
Button / Size S on the group shrinks every child, so the labels fit again.

content.title: Short, related actions in a clear order
content.description: Keep a group to a few actions that belong together. End with the action people are most likely to choose.
blocks: Supporting actions come first. Only Pay sets a stronger Emphasis mode, so it stands out.
An IconButton without a label is announced by its icon name, such as “Qr Code”. Specify a task-based label, such as “Scan QR code”, for each icon action.
Button labels stay on one line. When the share is too narrow, the end of the label is cut off with an ellipsis.

inContext.title: Settle a shared bill
inContext.description: A Coin Card holds the context. The ButtonGroup keeps split, request, and pay together, with Pay emphasized.
blocks: Choose how to settle the bill.

doDont.title: Keep the row readable
doDont.description: Most problems come from missing width or conflicting modes on individual children.
blocks: In a 300 px host, both Buttons have room for their labels.
Let the group shrink to its content
Without a host width, the Buttons divide the smallest possible row and “Request” is cut short.
Set the size once on the group
Every child inherits Button / Size M, so the row keeps one height.
Pay’s own Button / Size S wins over the group mode and leaves one short, mismatched action.
Only Pay sets Emphasis High, so the next step is obvious.
With Emphasis High on the group, all three actions compete for attention.

sources.title: Public ButtonGroup, verified behavior
sources.description: The guide renders the public jfs-components ButtonGroup with public IconButton and Button children.
blocks: Button group master, node 2018:4119 · no exposed properties
ButtonGroup docs, default, mixed-children, and modes stories

Declared, installed, and npm latest are all jfs-components@0.1.60. The Figma master is a 150 × 42 row of three icon actions with Button / Size M, Emphasis Medium, and AppearanceBrand Primary. The package renders each IconButton at 40 px, so the same row measures 144 × 40. In Storybook, the default story’s third icon (ic_menu) is missing from the icon registry, and the modes story passes a token name that ButtonGroup does not read.
